questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How karaoke became popular in Japan
How to become a professional singer
Why guitars are easier to play than singing
Singing, and why it helps even bad singers
questions.why: They discuss what happens when we sing and why it's not essential to sing in tune to benefit.

questions.q: What does Georgina think about Neil's singing?
options: She thinks he sings beautifully
She thinks he might be tone deaf
She thinks he should sing opera
She has never heard him sing
questions.why: She says after hearing him at the Christmas party, 'I think you might be tone deaf'.

questions.q: How does Neil feel about his own singing?
options: He loves it and makes up for his lack of skill with enthusiasm
He is embarrassed by his voice and wants to stop singing
He thinks he is easily the best singer in the whole office
He only ever sings when he is alone in the shower at home
questions.why: Neil says, 'what I lack in ability, I make up for in enthusiasm!'

questions.q: According to Marijke Peters, what decides how high or low a sung note is?
options: The size of your lungs
How loudly you sing
How fast the vocal folds vibrate
The shape of your mouth
questions.why: She says the pitch depends on the frequency of the vocal folds' vibration.

questions.q: Why do the presenters compare singing to playing a guitar?
options: Because most singers also play the guitar
Because both need a lot of practice
Because guitars are made from similar materials
Because both use vibration to make sound
questions.why: They say the vocal cords act like strings and the larynx, like the guitar's body, amplifies the sound.

questions.q: According to Professor Peter Pfordresher, where is the problem for most poor singers?
options: In their ears and how they hear music
In their voice
In how the brain links sound and muscles
In their lungs
questions.why: Neil says he thinks it's not the ears or voice, but the brain's connection between sound perception and muscle movement.

questions.q: What does Professor Pfordresher advise people who don't sing well?
options: Keep singing, because it has social and stress benefits
Take lessons with a teacher before singing in public
Only sing along with a backing track to help them
Stop singing completely to protect their voice from damage
questions.why: He recommends to 'keep singing' because it benefits people socially and for stress responses.

questions.q: Why does Neil say Georgina has 'changed her tune'?
options: She started singing a different song
She now thinks maybe he should keep singing
She decided to learn the guitar
She now says karaoke is boring
questions.why: After criticising him, Georgina says, 'maybe you should keep singing, after all!'
